fixes.explanation: Samuel never mentions banishment. His words are, “Saul will hear of it and kill me!” That's a heavy moment, friend. The LORD answers Samuel and gives him something to do about it.

Right, they ask, “Do you come in peace?” They tremble when they ask it. Samuel answers, “In peace,” and then tells them he has come to sacrifice to the LORD. A little trembling in front of a prophet is something I understand, friend, because my mustache does it when the oven timer goes off.
The elders don't ask about Saul. They tremble and ask, “Do you come in peace?” Their question is about Samuel himself. Samuel answers, “In peace.”
They don't ask about anyone else. The elders meet Samuel trembling and ask, “Do you come in peace?” Samuel answers with “In peace,” and then says he has come to sacrifice to the LORD.
Not quite, friend. The text says Samuel “…consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.” So the sons are consecrated and invited right along with their father.
Samuel says nothing about Eliab being too young. His words are, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.” I think he's seeing a king, not a problem. And the LORD answers him next.

The family line isn't in His words. The LORD says, “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” He sets outward appearance next to the heart. Earlier He tells Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height…”

Five is short. The text says Jesse “…made seven of his sons pass before Samuel…” That's two more than you counted, and still not the chosen one. Samuel tells him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”

Ten is too many. The text says Jesse “…made seven of his sons pass before Samuel…” After that, Jesse says there is still the youngest, who is tending the sheep. So seven is the count of sons who pass before Samuel.
True. Samuel says, “Send for him… For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.” The meal waits for the youngest. I'd say that's some serious confidence from Samuel.
The text says the opposite. Samuel says, “Send for him… For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.” So the eating waits for the youngest.

That's what the LORD says: “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.” After seven sons and a wait, the answer is plain. The LORD tells Samuel which one, just like He said He would. I think the whole room was holding its breath, like when the oven door opens.

The Spirit of the LORD. The text says, “…the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.” David is the youngest son, the one who was tending the sheep. Samuel anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day forward the Spirit rushed upon him.
